name: Rise account module execute without access control
summary: Rise account 0xc851e5a0, a registry-routed clone that solely owned several Rise vaults, exposed execute(operation, target, value, data) with no caller check. Anyone could make it call a vault's owner-only payout (0xaaa18f86) routing the balance to themselves. The attacker drained two vaults on Ethereum, then the account's twin on Base; a copycat took a later Base deposit.
notes: Same-address account clones on Ethereum and Base resolve key 0xa487ef87 to modules 0xb1a4010d and 0xa2362ea5, both open to any caller since each clone's creation (eth_call from an unrelated address passes; the module frame reads no caller). The Ethereum leg came two hours before the Base one, so it anchors.

The vaults' owner-only payout works as designed and naming the account as owner only set exposure, so the vaults and their later code routes (Ethereum vault key changed at block 24312917) are not targets. Copycat 0x359e11ab, unaffiliated, swept a 100,000 USDC deposit on Base.
